# ciphertrust_property (Resource)

Manages a CipherTrust Manager system property. **Only available on CipherTrust Manager — not supported on CDSPaaS, where system properties are managed by the platform.**

The `name` attribute is the resource identifier and is **immutable** — changing it after creation produces a plan-time error. To manage a different property, remove the resource from state (`terraform state rm`) and create a new one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Terraform Configuration for CipherTrust Provider

# This configuration demonstrates the updation of a CipherTrust Manager property resource
# with the CipherTrust provider, including setting up property details.

terraform {
  # Define the required providers for the configuration
  required_providers {
    # CipherTrust provider for managing CipherTrust resources
    ciphertrust = {
      # The source of the provider
      source = "ThalesGroup/CipherTrust"
      # Version of the provider to use
      version = "1.0.0-pre3"
    }
  }
}

# Configure the CipherTrust provider for authentication
provider "ciphertrust" {
	# The address of the CipherTrust appliance (replace with the actual address)
  address = "https://10.10.10.10"

  # Username for authenticating with the CipherTrust appliance
  username = "admin"

  # Password for authenticating with the CipherTrust appliance
  password = "ChangeMe101!"
}

# Add a resource of type CipherTrust Manager property with the name ENABLE_RECORDS_DB_STORE
resource "ciphertrust_property" "property_1" {
    name = "ENABLE_RECORDS_DB_STORE"
    value = "false"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `name` (String) **(Immutable)** Name of the system property used as the resource identifier. Changing this field after creation produces a plan-time error.
- `value` (String) Value to be set

### Read-Only

- `description` (String) Description of the property and its value (read-only from API)

## Behavioral Notes

- **Delete is a no-op for resource removal:** `terraform destroy` removes the resource from Terraform state but calls the CM reset endpoint (`POST /v1/system/properties/<name>/reset`) to restore the property to its default value. System properties are permanent fixtures and cannot be deleted.
- **Drift detection:** Changes to a property's value outside Terraform surface as plan drift on the next `terraform plan`.
- **Safe test property:** `ALLOW_UNKNOWN_FIELDS` with values `"false"`/`"true"` is confirmed writable and safe for automated tests.
